code_actions.rationale: No documentation in progress notes or discharge diagnoses explicitly supports a diagnosis of anoxic brain damage; cognitive impairment is attributed to HSV encephalitis in the chart, so G93.1 is unsupported and removed.
The chart documents new post-encephalitis cognitive impairment and memory problems but does not document pre-existing dementia with behavioral disturbance; remove F02.81 as unsupported.
Vascular dementia is not supported by the chart (H&P documents previously healthy, and discharge attributes cognitive impairment to encephalitis); remove.

Chart documents a catheter-associated right internal jugular DVT but does not explicitly document an insertion procedure of an infusion device into the superior vena cava; insufficient specific documentation to support this exact PCS (remove unless operative/procedure note supports).

The chart contains conflicting documentation about tracheostomy approach (H&P problem list documents 'Percutaneous tracheostomy' while the billed PCS is for open tracheostomy). Because approach determines correct PCS, remove 0B110F4 pending clinician clarification; human adjudication required.

evidence.quote: Principal Diagnosis Refractory status epilepticus; HSV-1 encephalitis
The patient was intubated for airway protection with escalation of anticonvulsants and empiric acyclovir initiation given clinical suspicion for HSV encephalitis.
CSF HSV-1 PCR was positive and MRI demonstrated bilateral temporal lobe changes characteristic of HSV encephalitis; a full 21-day course of intravenous acyclovir was completed.
New-onset refractory status epilepticus secondary to HSV encephalitis
Interval: sputum culture growing Streptococcus pneumoniae; narrowing antibiotics; continuing HSV encephalitis treatment NAEON; cont current Rx 2/2 critical illness.
prolonged mechanical ventilation requiring tracheostomy on ICU day 14, PEG placement for enteral nutrition on ICU day 16, and profound ICU-acquired weakness.
catheter-associated right internal jugular DVT treated with therapeutic anticoagulation
ABG (02:00): pH 7.28 / PaCO2 45 / PaO2 66 / HCO3 18; lactate 5.2 mmol/L; P/F ratio 73.

Discharge / Transfer Diagnoses Resolved refractory status epilepticus; treated HSV-1 encephalitis; ongoing cognitive impairment from encephalitis; residual right-sided weakness; resolved aspiration pneumonia (S. pneumoniae); tracheostomy-dependent respiratory status (trach collar); catheter-associated right internal jugular DVT on anticoagulation; resolved SIADH; ICU-acquired weakness.

system_note: This DRG review examined all billed diagnoses and procedures against the chart. Summary of key findings and supporting documentation: 1) Principal diagnosis sequencing: the medical record consistently documents refractory status epilepticus as the condition that occasioned admission and HSV-1 encephalitis as the underlying cause (supporting sequencing status epilepticus as principal). See ev4 (Discharge/Transfer Summary: Admission Diagnoses: New-onset refractory status epilepticus secondary to HSV encephalitis) and ev1 (H&P: Principal Diagnosis Refractory status epilepticus; HSV-1 encephalitis). Based on these notes, the principal diagnosis should be G41.0 (refractory status epilepticus) rather than B00.4 first. (evidence: ev4, ev1). 2) HSV-1 encephalitis is well-supported and present on admission: CSF HSV-1 PCR positive and MRI with bilateral temporal lobe changes; empiric acyclovir was started on presentation (evidence: ev3, ev2). Keep B00.4 as a secondary diagnosis, POA=Y. 3) Several billed secondary diagnoses are supported by the record and should be retained (acute respiratory failure, coma, aspiration pneumonia with Streptococcus pneumoniae, SIADH, catheter-associated right IJ DVT, anterograde amnesia, right-sided hemiparesis/hemiplegia, ventilator dependence): evidence includes admission/ICU notes, microbiology and progress notes, and the discharge/transfer summary (evidence: ev10 for respiratory failure ABG/P/F values; ev5 and ev6 for S. pneumoniae aspiration pneumonia; ev9 for catheter-associated right internal jugular DVT; ev7 for tracheostomy and PEG). 4) Diagnoses without adequate chart support (remove): G93.1 (anoxic brain damage) - the chart and the discharge diagnoses attribute the cognitive deficits to HSV encephalitis and post-encephalitis impairment rather than a documented anoxic brain injury; there is no progress note or discharge problem explicitly diagnosing anoxic brain damage (evidence: ev11 [the discharge diagnoses list shows post-encephalitis cognitive impairment and does not list anoxic brain damage] and ev3/ev4 showing HSV encephalitis as the explanatory cause). 5) Duplicate / unsupported dementia codes: both F02.81 (dementia in other diseases with behavioral disturbance) and F03.B0 (vascular dementia) are billed; the record documents new post-encephalitis cognitive impairment and memory impairment but documents the patient as previously healthy with no prior dementia (H&P). There is no documentation supporting pre-existing vascular dementia (remove F02.81 and F03.B0) (evidence: ev1 and ev11). 6) Procedure-level conflict (human review required): billed tracheostomy code is 0B110F4 (open tracheostomy). The H&P problem list explicitly records "Percutaneous tracheostomy for prolonged coma" while the chart elsewhere documents that a tracheostomy was performed on ICU day 14 but does not clearly state approach. This is a direct conflict between the clinical documentation lines and the billed PCS approach (see CONFLICT-00121). Because the approach (percutaneous vs open) determines the correct ICD-10-PCS code, this requires human adjudication before retaining 0B110F4 or substituting the appropriate percutaneous tracheostomy code (evidence: ev8 and ev7). 7) Other procedures (endotracheal intubation on admission, LP, PEG, EEG monitoring, prolonged ventilation >96 hours) are documented and supported (evidence: ev2, ev3, ev7). Correction summary (claim-level): - Change principal diagnosis to G41.0 (Grand mal status epilepticus) - role principal; POA=Y; severity=MCC. - Keep B00.4 (Herpesviral encephalitis) as secondary; POA=Y; severity=MCC (supported by positive CSF PCR and MRI). - Remove G93.1 (anoxic brain damage) - unsupported in the record. - Remove F02.81 and F03.B0 (dementia codes) - unsupported / contradicted by admission H&P and discharge summary which attribute cognitive deficits to encephalitis, not pre-existing dementia. - Retain acute respiratory failure (J96.01), unspecified coma (R40.9), aspiration pneumonia (J69.0) and pneumonia due to S. pneumoniae (J13), SIADH (E22.2), catheter-associated right IJ DVT (I82.C11), anterograde amnesia (R41.1), right hemiplegia (G81.94), Z99.11 ventilator dependence, and procedures for intubation, LP, PEG, EEG monitoring, and prolonged ventilation >96 hours. - Remove billed open tracheostomy 0B110F4 pending human confirmation of surgical approach (open vs percutaneous); if percutaneous approach is confirmed, the PCS should be recoded accordingly. Evidence relied on (document/section/page are provided from the citations below): ev1, ev2, ev3, ev4, ev5, ev6, ev7, ev8, ev9, ev10. Because the tracheostomy approach is unresolved in the record (CONFLICT-00121) this review is a Finding and requires human escalation to confirm PCS approach before final procedure-list coding. Detailed evidence citations are in evidence_cited. Principal diagnosis: the review proposed G41.0 in place of the billed B00.4. Nothing in the record contradicts B00.4 independently, so it is kept as the principal and G41.0 as a secondary diagnosis; a reviewer should confirm the principal.
rationale_letter: To: Medical Records/Coding Department Re: MR_16 - DRG-level audit determination We performed a full DRG-level audit of the above inpatient stay, comparing the billed diagnosis and procedure set to the medical record documentation. Findings: After review of the chart (H&P, progress notes, consult notes, and discharge/transfer summary), we find that the principal diagnosis sequencing and several secondary diagnoses require correction, and one procedure requires clinician clarification before the hospital may substantiate its PCS coding. Basis for determination (selected chart evidence): - The chart documents "New-onset refractory status epilepticus secondary to HSV encephalitis" and the H&P lists the principal diagnosis as refractory status epilepticus with HSV-1 encephalitis (see Discharge/Transfer Summary Admission Diagnoses and H&P, ev4 and ev1). This supports sequencing G41.0 (status epilepticus) as principal rather than B00.4 first. - HSV-1 encephalitis is confirmed in the record: CSF HSV-1 PCR positive and MRI with bilateral temporal lobe changes; a full intravenous acyclovir course was completed (see ev3). Keep B00.4 as a secondary diagnosis, POA=Y. - Aspiration pneumonia with Streptococcus pneumoniae is documented in progress and consult notes (sputum culture growing S. pneumoniae, targeted antibiotics), supporting J69.0 and J13 as secondary diagnoses (see ev5, ev6). - Tracheostomy and PEG placement are documented; prolonged mechanical ventilation is documented and supports the >96-hour ventilation procedure code (see ev7). - The record does not contain authoritative documentation of anoxic brain damage (G93.1). The discharge diagnoses attribute cognitive deficits to HSV encephalitis / post-encephalitis impairment rather than an anoxic brain injury; no note explicitly diagnoses anoxic brain damage. Therefore G93.1 is unsupported and will be removed. - Two billed dementia codes (F02.81 and F03.B0) are not supported by the chart: the patient is documented as previously healthy with new cognitive impairment related to encephalitis, not pre-existing vascular dementia or established dementia; those codes will be removed. - The billed ICD-10-PCS for tracheostomy (0B110F4 - open tracheostomy) conflicts with a contemporaneous clinical line that documents "Percutaneous tracheostomy for prolonged coma" (H&P problem list). Because PCS approach (open vs percutaneous) materially changes the correct code, we require clinician clarification (CONFLICT-00121). Action taken: - Principal diagnosis recoded to G41.0 (Grand mal status epilepticus) - principal, POA=Y, severity=MCC. - B00.4 (Herpesviral encephalitis) retained as secondary, POA=Y, severity=MCC. - Removed diagnoses: G93.1 (anoxic brain damage), F02.81 (dementia in other diseases w/ behavioral disturbance), F03.B0 (vascular dementia). - Retained secondary diagnoses supported by the chart: R40.9, J96.01, J69.0, J13, E22.2, I82.C11, R41.1, G81.94, Z99.11. - Procedures retained: endotracheal intubation, lumbar puncture, PEG, EEG monitoring, prolonged mechanical ventilation (>96 hours). - Procedure 0B110F4 (open tracheostomy) removed pending clinician clarification of percutaneous vs open approach; recoding to the correct PCS will be completed on receipt of clarification. Please provide written clarification (operative report or procedural note) stating the tracheostomy approach (open vs percutaneous) and the date the procedure was performed. If an operative/procedure note confirms an open tracheostomy, we will reinstate 0B110F4; if percutaneous, we will substitute the appropriate PCS code. Thank you. Sincerely, Clinical Claims Auditor
